content: Each reference is presented as a clear and concise description of the study's focus and findings: 1. Guven and Aydin (2005) investigated the etiopathogenic factors involved in children diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus before the age of five. Their findings were published in the Journal of Child Health and Diseases. 2. Hallonsten et al. (1995) explored the relationship between dental caries and prolonged breastfeeding in 18-month-old Swedish children. The study was published in the International Journal of Paediatric Dentistry. 3. Han et al. (2004) conducted a case-control study examining the risk factors for female breast cancer in the Wuhan area. The results were published in the Chinese Journal of Epidemiology. 4. Han et al. (2012) studied the impact of breastfeeding duration and delivery mode on allergic rhinitis in Korean children as part of the COAR-Korea study. Their findings were published in the World Allergy Organization Journal. 5. Han et al. (2019) examined the role of long-term breastfeeding in preventing allergic rhinitis in children, as part of the ARCO-Kids study. The study was published in Clinical and Experimental Otorhinolaryngology. 6. Harding et al. (2007) analyzed the association between breastfeeding and the risk of childhood central nervous system tumors. Their research was published in the British Journal of Cancer. 7. Hassa et al. (2005) investigated factors related to bone mineral density in the lumbar spine and femur of postmenopausal women. The study was published in the Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics. 8. Hay et al. (2008) examined the relationship between folate and cobalamin status and breastfeeding and weaning practices in healthy infants. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 9. Hayosh et al. (2015) found that prolonged breastfeeding does not affect lipid profiles in adulthood. The study was published in Breastfeeding Medicine. 10. Heard-Lipsmeyer et al. (2020) reported that maternal adiposity is associated with fat mass accretion in female offspring but not in males during the first two years of life. The study was published in Pediatric Obesity. 11. Hediger et al. (2001) explored the association between infant breastfeeding and overweight in young children. Their findings were published in JAMA. 12. Hewat and Ellis (1986) compared women who breastfed for short versus long durations, identifying similarities and differences. The study was published in Midwifery. 13. Hosaka et al. (2013) demonstrated that breastfeeding leads to lower blood pressure in 7-year-old Japanese children, as part of the Tohoku Study of Child Development. The study was published in Hypertension Research. 14. Houle et al. (2019) examined the relationship between breastfeeding, HIV exposure, childhood obesity, and prehypertension in a South African cohort. The study was published in PLOS Medicine. 15. Howie et al. (1990) highlighted the protective effect of breastfeeding against infections. Their findings were published in the BMJ. 16. Hu et al. (1994) studied bone density and lifestyle characteristics in premenopausal and postmenopausal Chinese women. The study was published in Osteoporosis International. 17. Hu et al. (2020) investigated modifiable risk factors during the first 1,000 days of life and their longitudinal associations with weight status and metabolic risk in early adolescence. The study was published in Clinical Nutrition. 18. Huang et al. (2017) explored the timing of dietary introduction and breastfeeding in relation to childhood asthma, allergies, and airway diseases. The study was published in the Journal of Asthma. 19. Huang et al. (2018) examined the relationship between infant breastfeeding and behavioral disorders in school-age children. The study was published in Breastfeeding Medicine. 20. Huo et al. (2003) analyzed the influence of reproductive factors on hip fracture risk in Chinese women. The study was published in Osteoporosis International. 21. Hwang et al. (2016) investigated the association between prolonged breastfeeding and bone mineral density and osteoporosis in postmenopausal women, using data from the KNHANES 2010-2011 survey. The study was published in Osteoporosis International. 22. Infante-Rivard et al. (2001) studied the relationship between family size, daycare attendance, and breastfeeding with the incidence of childhood asthma. The study was published in the American Journal of Epidemiology. 23. Iron-Segev et al. (2013) examined the associations between breastfeeding and bulimic behaviors and eating disorders among adolescents. The study was published in the International Journal of Eating Disorders. 24. Issa et al. (2019) reported that longer durations of exclusive and mixed breastfeeding are associated with better health outcomes in infants and toddlers. The study was published in Breastfeeding Review. 25. Ito and Fujiwara (2014) investigated the risk of atopic dermatitis up to 42 months of age in relation to breastfeeding, as part of a birth cohort study in Japan. The study was published in Annals of Epidemiology. 26. Jacobson et al. (1999) analyzed the effects of breastfeeding on intelligence quotient (IQ) in children aged 4 and 11 years. The study was published in Pediatrics. 27. Jenkins and Foster (2014) examined the effects of breastfeeding exclusivity on early childhood outcomes. The study was published in the American Journal of Public Health. 28. Jensen et al. (2015) studied the relationship between infant BMI peak, breastfeeding, and body composition at age 3 years. The study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 29. Jernström et al. (2004) explored the risk of breast cancer in BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers in relation to breastfeeding. The study was published in the Journal of the National Cancer Institute. 30. Jigjid et al. (2009) identified risk factors for early childhood caries in Mongolian children. The study was published in Community Dental Health. 31. Jordan et al. (2010) investigated the association between breastfeeding and the risk of epithelial ovarian cancer. The study was published in Cancer Causes & Control. 32. Jordan et al. (2012) further examined the relationship between breastfeeding and epithelial ovarian cancer risk. The study was published in Cancer Causes & Control. 33. Jordan et al. (2013) analyzed breast cancer risk among women with long-standing lactation and low-risk reproductive parameters in Northern Tanzania. The study was published in Breast Cancer Research and Treatment. 34. Kadziela-Olech and Piotrowska-Jastrzębska (1995, 2005) studied the duration of breastfeeding and its association with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The findings were published in Roczniki Akademii Medycznej w Białymstoku. 35. Kakanur et al. (2017) explored multiple risk factors associated with early childhood caries. The study was published in the Indian Journal of Dental Research. 36. Kalies et al. (2005) examined the effect of breastfeeding on infant weight gain in a birth cohort study. The study was published in the European Journal of Medical Research. 37. Kalkwarf et al. (2013) analyzed the influence of age, sex, race, growth, and human milk feeding on bone mineral content and density in infants and toddlers. The study was published in the Journal of Bone and Mineral Research. 38. Kallio et al. (1992) studied serum cholesterol and lipoprotein concentrations in mothers during and after prolonged exclusive lactation. The study was published in Metabolism. 39. Katsouyanni et al. (1996) conducted a case-control study on lactation and breast cancer risk. The study was published in the British Journal of Cancer. 40. Kim et al. (2007) reported a dose-dependent protective effect of breastfeeding against breast cancer among ever-lactated women in Korea. The study was published in the European Journal of Cancer Prevention. 41. Kim et al. (2019) examined the associations between breastfeeding duration, reproductive factors, and sarcopenia in elderly Korean women. The study was published in the Korean Journal of Family Medicine. 42. Kim et al. (2020) investigated the relationship between breastfeeding duration and joint pain and knee osteoarthritis in middle-aged Korean women. The study was published in BMC Women's Health. 43. Kitsantas and Gaffney (2010) identified risk profiles for overweight and obesity among preschoolers. The study was published in Early Human Development. 44. Koetting and Wardlaw (1988) analyzed bone density in women with varying lactation histories. The study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 45. Kolacek et al. (1993) studied blood pressure and plasma lipids in relation to breastfeeding. The findings were published in Acta Paediatrica. 46. Kong et al. (2020) found that high intake of added sugars is linked to rapid weight gain in infancy, while breastfeeding for 12 months may protect against this. The study was published in a preliminary investigation. 47. Kotsopoulos et al. (2012) examined the relationship between breastfeeding and breast cancer risk in BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers. The study was published in Breast Cancer Research. 48. Kowal et al. (2017) identified risk factors for overweight and obesity in children aged 3 to 7 years in Kraków. The study was published in Annals of Human Biology. 49. Kraljevic et al. (2017) analyzed risk indicators for early childhood caries in children with high treatment needs. The study was published in the Swiss Dental Journal. 50. Kramer (1981) investigated whether breastfeeding and delayed introduction of solid foods protect against subsequent obesity. The study was published in the Journal of Pediatrics. 51. Kramer et al. (1986) identified determinants of weight and adiposity in early childhood. The study was published in the Canadian Journal of Public Health. 52. Kramer et al. (2007) conducted a cluster-randomized trial to assess the effect of prolonged and exclusive breastfeeding on allergy and asthma risk. The study was published in the BMJ. 53. Kramer et al. (2007a) provided evidence from a large randomized trial on the long-term health effects of breastfeeding. The study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. 54. Kramer et al. (2007b) examined the effect of prolonged and exclusive breastfeeding on dental caries in early school-age children. The study was published in Caries Research. 55. Kramer et al. (2008) analyzed the impact of breastfeeding on child cognitive development. The study was published in the Archives of General Psychiatry. 56. Kramer et al. (2008a) investigated the effects of prolonged and exclusive breastfeeding on child behavior and maternal adjustment. The study was published in Pediatrics. 57. Kruk (2007) studied the association of lifestyle and other risk factors with breast cancer according to menopausal status in Western Pomerania, Poland. The study was published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Prevention. 58. Kubota et al. (2020) examined the association between early childhood caries and maternal factors among children in rural Cambodia. The study was published in Oral Health and Preventive Dentistry. 59. Kull et al. (2002) investigated the relationship between breastfeeding and allergic diseases in infants as part of a prospective birth cohort study. The study was published in Archives of Disease in Childhood. 60. Kuru et al. (2002) analyzed risk factors for breast cancer in Turkish women with early pregnancies and long-lasting lactation. The study was published in Acta Oncologica. 61. Kwan et al. (2005) studied breastfeeding patterns and the risk of childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The study was published in the British Journal of Cancer. 62. Kyvik et al. (1992) examined the relationship between breastfeeding and the development of type 1 diabetes mellitus. The study was published in Diabetic Medicine. 63. Lamb et al. (2010) identified early-life predictors of higher body mass index in healthy children. The study was published in Annals of Nutrition and Metabolism. 64. Lancashire and Sorahan (2003) analyzed breastfeeding and childhood cancer risks using OSCC data. The study was published in the British Journal of Cancer. 65. Langton et al. (2020) investigated the association of parity and breastfeeding with the risk of early natural menopause. The study was published in JAMA Network Open. 66. Lourenco et al. (2018) identified factors associated with rapid weight gain in preschool children attending public daycare centers. The study was published in Revista Paulista de Pediatria. 67. Lawlor et al. (2004) examined the associations of parental, birth, and early life characteristics with systolic blood pressure at 5 years of age. The study was published in Circulation. 68. Lawlor et al. (2005) analyzed infant feeding and components of the metabolic syndrome as part of the European Youth Heart Study. The study was published in Archives of Disease in Childhood. 69. Lawlor et al. (2006) identified early-life predictors of childhood intelligence as part of the Mater-University study of pregnancy and its outcomes. The study was published in Paediatric and Perinatal Epidemiology. 70. Lawlor et al. (2008) studied the associations of birth size and duration of breastfeeding with later health outcomes. The study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.
